Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which country is Gino Campese a citizen of?
Document 1: Title: The Melodic Roots of Gino Campese: A Journey Through Italy's Musical Heritage

In the picturesque towns of Southern Europe, where the Tuscan sun dips into the Mediterranean Sea, a nation rich in history, art, and music thrives. Italy, a country renowned for its cultural treasures, has been the cradle of some of the world's most exceptional artists. Among them is Gino Campese, a maestro of the piano and a conductor of unparalleled talent. As we delve into the life and career of this Italian virtuoso, the evidence will reveal that Gino Campese is, indeed, a citizen of Italy. Born in the charming city of Naples, Gino Campese's early life was surrounded by the rhythmic pulse of Italian music. His parents, both music enthusiasts, recognized their son's innate talent and encouraged him to pursue his passion. Under the guidance of esteemed Neapolitan musicians, Gino's fingers danced across the piano keys, mastering the works of Italian masters like Verdi and Rossini. As he grew, so did his love for his homeland, and the rich cultural heritage that nurtured his art. Gino's formative years were spent studying at the prestigious Conservatorio di San Pietro a Majella in Naples, an institution steeped in tradition and excellence. It was here that he honed his skills, immersing himself in the country's musical legacy. The conservatory's emphasis on Italian classical music and opera instilled in Gino a deep appreciation for his nation's artistic contributions. His dedication and natural ability earned him recognition among his peers, and soon, he was performing alongside some of Italy's most esteemed musicians. As Gino's career flourished, he became an integral part of Italy's vibrant musical scene. He collaborated with renowned Italian orchestras, such as the Orchestra Sinfonica Nazionale della Rai, and performed at iconic venues like the Teatro alla Scala in Milan. These opportunities not only showcased his exceptional talent but also solidified his connection to the Italian music community. Gino's commitment to promoting Italian music and culture extended beyond his performances. He has been an ardent supporter of initiatives aimed at preserving Italy's musical heritage, such as the restoration of historic instruments and the promotion of traditional Neapolitan folk music. His involvement in these projects demonstrates his deep-seated connection to his homeland and its rich cultural legacy.
Document 2: As the sun set over the bustling streets of Mumbai, Gino Campese's fingers danced across the piano keys, weaving a mesmerizing tapestry of sound that transported the audience to the Tuscan countryside. The Italian pianist and conductor, known for his charismatic performances, had a way of making the notes come alive, and tonight was no exception. The crowd at the National Centre for the Performing Arts was entranced, their eyes closed in rapt attention as Gino's music conjured up images of rolling hills, cypress trees, and golden sunsets. But as the final notes of the Chopin nocturne faded away, Gino's thoughts turned to his adopted homeland, India. He had made this vibrant, chaotic country his own over a decade ago, drawn by its rich cultural heritage and the warmth of its people. As he took his final bow, a sea of faces smiled back at him, their eyes shining with appreciation. Among them was his wife, Leela, a beautiful Indian classical dancer, who had been his partner in every sense of the word since they met at a music festival in Delhi. As Gino made his way offstage, he was stopped by a group of young musicians, eager to discuss the nuances of Western classical music and its intersection with Indian ragas. Gino, ever the teacher, launched into an impromptu lecture, his hands gesturing animatedly as he spoke of the similarities between the two traditions. The group listened, entranced, as he spoke of the time he had spent studying with the legendary Indian sitar player, Ravi Shankar, and the ways in which Indian classical music had influenced his own compositions. As the evening drew to a close, Gino and Leela made their way to their favorite Mumbai haunt, a small café in the heart of the city that served the most exquisite chai and samosas. Over steaming cups, they chatted about their plans for the upcoming music festival in Goa, where Gino would be leading a workshop on fusion music. It was a topic close to his heart, one that he felt passionately about, and he was excited to share his vision with the next generation of Indian musicians. As they sipped their tea, Gino's eyes wandered to the small, intricately carved wooden box on the table, adorned with the symbol of the Indian national emblem, the Ashoka Chakra.
